subject: pathology
title: Reversible Cell Injury, Cellular Swelling, and Ultrastructural Derangements

steps.tx: When environmental stresses or metabolic insults overwhelm normal homeostatic limits, cells undergo a spectrum of morphological and functional alterations. If the injurious stimulus is mild or transient, the cell experiences **reversible cell injury**, during which functional derangements and structural abnormalities can completely normalize once the offending etiology is removed.
steps.say: Reversible cell injury occurs when transient stress causes changes that completely resolve once the stress ceases.

nodes.label: Acute Hypoxia or Toxin Depresses Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation
Intracellular ATP Generation Plummets, Paralyzing Energy-Dependent Pumps
Intracellular Sodium and Water Accumulate while Potassium Leaks out
Oxygen Reintroduction Restores Respiration, Returning Cell to Normal Homeostasis

steps.tx: When stress passes ordinary homeostatic limits, cells show a range of structural and functional changes. If the insult is mild or brief, the result is **reversible cell injury**, and both function and structure can return to normal once the cause is gone. Cloudy swelling is that state under the microscope: cells look pale and swollen from excess water, the endoplasmic reticulum dilates, and these hydropic changes recede if oxygenation and ATP are restored before membranes fail for good.
steps.say: Mild or short lived stress produces reversible cell injury, which can normalise completely after the cause is removed. Cloudy swelling is the visible form: pale, waterlogged cells with dilated endoplasmic reticulum. Those hydropic changes retreat if energy supply returns before membrane injury becomes permanent.

vis.alt: Pale swollen cells of cloudy swelling, with watery cytoplasm and dilated endoplasmic reticulum in reversible injury.
vis.caption: Hydropic cells look pale and enlarged, and their endoplasmic reticulum is dilated while the injury is still reversible. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The earliest and most universal morphological manifestation of almost all forms of cellular injury is generalized cell enlargement. Also designated **cloudy swelling**, this gross change produces pale, turgid organs with increased weight and rounded capsule margins due to impaired plasma membrane sodium-potassium adenosine triphosphatase pumps.
steps.say: Cloudy swelling is the earliest manifestation of injury, making affected organs pale, swollen, and heavy.

vis.alt: Cloudy swelling with pale swollen hydropic cells and dilated endoplasmic reticulum in reversible injury
vis.caption: Cloudy swelling with pale swollen hydropic cells and dilated endoplasmic reticulum in reversible injury. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: As water continues to rush into damaged cells along with sodium ions, the cytoplasm becomes distended with small clear vacuoles representing distended segments of the endoplasmic reticulum. Known microscopically as **hydropic change**, this severe form of intracellular oedema represents an advanced yet still reversible stage of cellular injury.
steps.say: Hydropic change occurs when water distends endoplasmic reticulum cisternae into clear cytoplasmic vacuoles.

left.title: Microscopic Hydropic Features
points: Cytoplasm displays numerous clear microvacuoles of water
Endoplasmic reticulum cisternae swell, pinch off, and dilate
Nucleus remains normally centered with intact chromatin pattern
Cell boundaries expand without plasma membrane rupture

right.title: Ultrastructural Alterations
points: Mitochondrial swelling with small amorphous calcium densities
Detachment of ribosomes from rough endoplasmic reticulum
Loss and distortion of microvilli along apical membranes
Formation of surface blebs and myelin figures from membranes

steps.tx: Under the transmission electron microscope, cells undergoing reversible injury reveal distinct organellar defects. Ribosomes detach from the rough endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria exhibit moderate matrix expansion, and the plasma membrane forms outpouchings termed **membrane blebs**, reflecting structural disruption of anchoring cortical actin cytoskeletal filaments.
steps.say: Reversible injury causes plasma membrane blebbing as actin filaments detach from the lipid bilayer.

nodes.label: ATP Exhaustion Inhibits Cytoskeletal Actin Polymerization
Cortical Microfilaments Detach from Plasma Membrane Anchors
Intracellular Hydrostatic Pressure Pushes Membrane Outward into Clear Blebs
Restoration of Energy Permitted Reabsorption of Blebs Without Lysis

steps.tx: Under the electron microscope, reversible injury detaches ribosomes from rough endoplasmic reticulum, expands the mitochondrial matrix only moderately, and pushes the plasma membrane into **membrane blebs** where cortical actin has lost its grip on the bilayer. The metabolic partner of that picture is energy failure. Oxidative phosphorylation stops, the cell falls back on anaerobic glycolysis, lactic acid accumulates, and intracellular pH falls, which is the setting in which those blebs and the ribosomal detachment appear.
steps.say: Reversible injury on electron microscopy shows ribosomes falling off rough endoplasmic reticulum, mild mitochondrial swelling, and plasma membrane blebs after actin detaches from the membrane. Behind those changes, aerobic respiration has failed. Anaerobic glycolysis takes over, lactate builds, and pH inside the cell drops.

vis.alt: A cell switching from aerobic respiration to anaerobic glycolysis, accumulating lactic acid as pH falls.
vis.caption: Blocked mitochondrial respiration forces glycolysis, lactate rises, and intracellular pH drops. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Mitochondrial dysfunction leads to an immediate switch from aerobic cellular respiration to anaerobic glycolysis. The subsequent accumulation of lactic acid and inorganic phosphates drops intracellular pH, inducing clumped nuclear chromatin and inactivating multiple metabolic enzymes, which further impairs **cellular energy metabolism** across damaged organelles.
steps.say: Anaerobic glycolysis generates lactic acid, lowering intracellular pH and clumping nuclear chromatin.

vis.alt: Cellular energy failure switching from aerobic respiration to anaerobic glycolysis with lactic acid accumulation and falling pH
vis.caption: Cellular energy failure switching from aerobic respiration to anaerobic glycolysis with lactic acid accumulation and falling pH. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: When metabolic or toxic insults persist past a critical threshold, biochemical changes pass a point of no return. The transition to **irreversible injury** is characterized by the permanent inability to reverse mitochondrial dysfunction and profound structural breakdown of plasma, lysosomal, and organellar membranes.
steps.say: Irreversible injury is defined by persistent mitochondrial failure and widespread membrane rupture.

left.title: Reversible Injury Hallmarks
points: Cellular swelling, cloudy swelling, and hydropic change
Mitochondrial swelling with preserved inner membrane potential
Ribosomal detachment and decreased protein synthesis
Nuclear chromatin clumping without structural fragmentation

right.title: Irreversible Injury Hallmarks
points: Opening of high-conductance mitochondrial permeability pores
Massive cytosolic influx of extracellular calcium ions
Severe rupture of plasma membrane with enzyme leakage into blood
Lysosomal membrane lysis and nuclear disintegration

steps.tx: A central hallmark of the transition to irreversible injury is the uncontrolled entry of calcium into the cytosol. Elevated intracellular calcium activates destructive endogenous enzymes, including phospholipases that degrade membrane lipids, proteases that dismantle cytoskeletal proteins, and endonucleases that fragment nuclear **chromatin DNA**.
steps.say: Massive cytosolic calcium influx activates phospholipases, proteases, and endonucleases that destroy the cell.

nodes.label: Loss of Calcium Homeostasis Permits Massive Influx from ECF and ER
Phospholipases Activated, Accelerating Membrane Phospholipid Degradation
Proteases Cleave Cytoskeletal Tubulin, Spectrin, and Actin Anchors
Endonucleases Fragment Chromosomal DNA, Precipitating Cell Death

steps.tx: Once plasma membrane integrity is breached, intracellular proteins and enzymes leak across the permeable membrane into the extracellular fluid and systemic circulation. Measuring these released macromolecules in serum provides sensitive clinical markers of tissue necrosis, such as cardiac troponins and creatine kinase-MB in **acute myocardial infarction**.
steps.say: Ruptured plasma membranes leak enzymes like troponin into blood, providing diagnostic markers of infarction.

nodes.label: Myocardial Sarcolemma Integrity Breaks Down Irreversibly
Cardiac Troponins I and T and CK-MB Diffuse into Interstitial Fluid

High-Sensitivity Serum Assays Detect Myocyte Death Within Hours
